findings: The frozen repository context contains three equivalent MySQL isolation-level questions, including the explicit default-level variant. The candidate answers all three directly and identifies InnoDB/MySQL transaction_isolation default as REPEATABLE READ.

The MySQL 8.4 primary-source packet supports all four level names and the key InnoDB mechanisms used in the answer: READ COMMITTED creates a fresh snapshot for each consistent read; REPEATABLE READ reuses the snapshot established by the first consistent read; SERIALIZABLE adds stronger locking semantics; READ UNCOMMITTED permits dirty/inconsistent reads.

The answer avoids a common weak pattern of reproducing only an ANSI anomaly table. It explains the RC-versus-RR difference through read-view lifetime, which directly accounts for why two ordinary SELECT statements in one RC transaction can observe later commits while RR consistent reads remain on one snapshot.

The candidate preserves the critical MySQL boundary between consistent nonlocking reads and locking reads/DML. It does not claim that all RR behavior comes only from MVCC or only from next-key locking, and it correctly presents record/gap/next-key locking as relevant to locking/range access paths.

The phantom-read discussion is appropriately qualified rather than making the absolute interview claim that RR universally eliminates every phantom across all read/write patterns. It distinguishes snapshot stability from current-data range locking.

The configuration boundary is useful and source-supported: default RR is not treated as proof that a particular application session currently runs at RR because transaction isolation can be overridden at global, session or next-transaction scope.

The answer does not fabricate throughput gains or production incidents and explicitly refuses to treat isolation level as a substitute for application read-modify-write concurrency protocols. The one-minute section is concise; the three-minute section is longer than literal oral timing, so oral quality is scored 4/5.
